scope: Diagnostic review of backend/ (RunningApp.*) against TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE v10. Read-only investigation. No backend files modified. No plan-catalog artifacts modified.
headlineFinding: Backend contains ZERO integration with plan-catalog. There is no code path that loads a plan-catalog bundle, JSON artifact, or any document keyed by TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE, GOAL_PACE_TEN_K, or any RUNTIME_CONDITION_VALUE. Backend generates previews exclusively from its own SQL database (PlanTemplates table, EF Core), seeded with exactly 3 rows, all 5K/Beginner. This makes most of the requested TD-D3-001/TD-WAVE5-001/schedule-safety questions not-yet-applicable rather than pass/fail -- the integration they presuppose does not exist yet.

question1_bundleLoading.evidence: grep -rli 'plan-catalog|plancatalog|TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE|GOAL_PACE|RUNTIME_CONDITION' across backend/**/*.cs and *.json returned zero matches (excluding bin/obj).
question1_bundleLoading.catalogBundleVersionCurrentlyConsumed: NONE -- no version of any plan-catalog bundle is consumed.
question1_bundleLoading.pinnedToOlderCandidateReasoning: Not pinned to an older version; never referenced any plan-catalog version at all.
question1_bundleLoading.dataSourceDetail: RunningApp.Domain.Entities.PlanTemplate has a free-form 'DataJson' string column ('serialized template weeks/days') in its own bespoke schema (templateId/version/goalType/goalDistance/level/daysPerWeek/unit/weeks[].days[].{slotIndex,dayType,distanceKm,durationMin,intensity}) -- structurally unrelated to any plan-catalog document type. Exactly 3 rows are seeded (baked into EF Core migrations, e.g. 20260624105830_InitialCreate.cs and carried through every subsequent migration snapshot): habit_5k_beginner_3day_km_v1, habit_5k_beginner_4day_km_v1, race_5k_beginner_3day_km_v1. All three are goalDistance=five_k, level=beginner. No 10K, no Intermediate, no 4-day-10K row exists anywhere in the seed data.
question1_bundleLoading.selectionLogic: PlaceholderPlanGenerationEngine.SelectTemplateAsync (src: RunningApp.Application/PlanGeneration/PlaceholderPlanGenerationEngine.cs) looks for an exact (GoalType, GoalDistance, Level, DaysPerWeek) match; if none found, it falls back to the FIRST seeded row (in whatever order EF returns) and reports FallbackUsed=true with an explicit reason string. A request for goal=Race, distance=TenK, level=(closest to Intermediate), daysPerWeek=4 would never match and would silently receive an arbitrary 5K/Beginner fallback template today.

question2_runtimeConditionMappingTdD3001.reasoning: PACE_SOURCE_IN, TIME_ADEQUACY_IN, CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN, and RuntimeConditionType as a concept do not exist anywhere in backend/ (zero grep matches for any of the three condition-type names, v1 or v2 values, in any *.cs file). Backend does not emit v2 canonical values because it never emits any RuntimeConditionType-shaped value at all. It also does not emit the old v1 strings (RACE_RESULT/TIME_TRIAL/NOT_PROVIDED/TIGHT/UNKNOWN) for the same reason. TD-D3-001 cannot be verified as 'satisfied' or 'violated' -- it is UNVERIFIABLE_BECAUSE_UNIMPLEMENTED.

readinessStandardInvestigation.producedWhere: NOT IN BACKEND. The string readiness="STANDARD" was found only in plan-catalog/docs/canonical/golden-fixture-v3/golden-10k-intermediate-4d-12w.v3.decisiontrace.json, a Golden Fixture example/reference document that lives under plan-catalog/docs, not in any backend source file.
readinessStandardInvestigation.fieldItBelongsTo: In that fixture document, it is CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_RESOLVER.evaluations[0].result.readiness -- a fixture-internal resolver output field, not a backend field. grep -rn '"STANDARD"' and grep -rn 'readiness' across backend/**/*.cs returned zero matches.
readinessStandardInvestigation.conflictsWithCoreEntryReadinessInV2: No conflict is possible because backend does not implement CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN at all. Within the fixture document itself (unaffected by this review), 'STANDARD' matches neither v1 (READY/NOT_READY/UNKNOWN) nor v2 (READY/CAUTION/NOT_READY) -- a pre-existing, already-documented fixture-vs-registry mismatch (see AUD-048, domain-d3-followup.md), not a new backend finding.
readinessStandardInvestigation.harmlessLegacyOrBug: N/A_TO_BACKEND -- this is a plan-catalog-fixture-internal question, already tracked as part of TD-D3-001's evidence in domain-d3-followup.md; no backend code produces or consumes this value.

question3_scheduleGenerationProof.scheduleGenerationDetail: PlanServices.GeneratePreviewAsync (RunningApp.Application/Services/PlanServices.cs) DOES turn a selected PlanTemplate's DataJson into a concrete weekly preview: it deserializes weeks/days, computes real calendar dates starting from the next Monday, and maps each day's slotIndex to a specific weekday via ResolvePreferredDays. This is real, working schedule-generation code -- but it operates entirely on the backend's own DataJson schema, never on any plan-catalog WorkoutProgression/RunLayout/ProgressionModifier document.
question3_scheduleGenerationProof.reasoning: GOAL_PACE_TEN_K is a plan-catalog WORKOUT_DEFINITION key. Backend's TemplateJsonData.days[].dayType is a free string compared against no plan-catalog vocabulary; the only 3 seeded templates contain dayType values 'easy', 'interval', 'long_run' -- 'goal_pace' (or any equivalent) does not appear in any seeded DataJson. Since GOAL_PACE_TEN_K cannot be selected as a template (no 10K/Intermediate template exists) and no seeded template's day content contains a goal-pace dayType, GOAL_PACE_TEN_K CANNOT currently appear in any backend-generated plan.
question3_scheduleGenerationProof.proofMethod: Static evidence (grep across all seeded DataJson strings in migrations + AppDbContext.cs for 'goal_pace'/'GOAL_PACE_TEN_K': zero matches), not a runtime-executed test, since there is no reachable code path to exercise for this specific workout.
question3_scheduleGenerationProof.weeksPhasesContainingGoalPace: NONE -- GOAL_PACE_TEN_K is unused by runtime despite being present in the plan-catalog catalog.
question3_scheduleGenerationProof.secondHardDayGenerated: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no goal-pace day is ever generated to create a conflict.
question3_scheduleGenerationProof.longRunSeparateFromGoalPace: UNKNOWN_FROM_CODE_EVIDENCE for the eventual real integration; for the CURRENT 5K/Beginner-only flow, long_run is a distinct dayType from easy/interval and is never merged with any hard-goal-pace concept (which doesn't exist in this schema).
question3_scheduleGenerationProof.taperProtection: UNKNOWN_FROM_CODE_EVIDENCE -- no seeded template contains a taper-labeled week (all 3 seeded templates have only 1 week of data: weekNumber=1, weekType='build'); no taper week-generation logic was found to inspect.

It is neither actively enforced nor declared-but-unused in backend -- it is simply absent, because backend has no concept of a ProgressionModifier at all.

allowSecondHardStimulus.reasoning: Same as above -- zero references anywhere in backend.

allowGoalPaceRehearsal.reasoning: Same as above -- zero references anywhere in backend. TD-WAVE5-001's question ('can goal-pace candidates be generated even when allowGoalPaceRehearsal=false') is not answerable in backend terms because backend has no allowGoalPaceRehearsal flag and, per question 3, cannot currently generate a goal-pace day regardless of any flag.

question4_hardSessionSafetyTdWave5001.note: This is a DIFFERENT and more fundamental gap than TD-WAVE5-001 as originally framed (which assumed a reachable goal-pace candidate in a real generation engine). The actual current state is that backend has neither the flag nor the candidate reachability it would guard -- both are absent, not merely unguarded.

missingEnumOrStringCases.detail: TrainingDayType {Easy, Interval, Tempo, LongRun, Rest, RecoveryEasy} has no case for a goal-pace-specific workout. Closest lossy fits are Tempo or Interval; no exact mapping exists.
Backend has no concept of a WorkoutProgression stage at all.
TrainingDayType conflates workout type and slot role into one flat enum with no 'key session' designation.
TrainingDayType.Easy / RecoveryEasy cover the workout-type dimension but there is no 'this is an EASY_SUPPORT slot' role concept distinct from any other easy run.
TrainingDayType.LongRun exists and is used in all 3 seeded templates (dayType='long_run').

TrainingWeekType enum {Base, Build, Recovery, Peak, Taper, RaceWeek} conceptually overlaps (Base~FOUNDATION, Build~BUILD, Peak~RACE_SPECIFIC, Taper~TAPER) but no exact 1:1 naming or mapping code exists between the two vocabularies; only 'build' is actually populated in any of the 3 seeded rows (all single-week templates).

missingEnumOrStringCases.concept: Workout intensity labels (e.g. GOAL_PACE intensity descriptor)
missingEnumOrStringCases.detail: Intensity is a free-form nullable string field (TrainingDay.Intensity, seen populated with zone labels like 'z2'/'z4') on every relevant entity/DTO -- structurally ABLE to carry a new label like 'goal_pace' without a schema change, but no mapping/translation code exists to populate it from a plan-catalog IntensityDescriptor today.

question6_outputApiCompatibility.conclusion: Missing/partial mappings confirmed for GOAL_PACE_TEN_K, GOAL_PACE_REHEARSAL, KEY_SESSION, and (partially) EASY_SUPPORT and phase names. LONG_RUN and free-text Intensity are structurally representable today.

finalClassificationReasoning: Not classified as BACKEND_BLOCKED_BY_RUNTIME_MAPPING specifically, because the runtime-condition-mapping question (TD-D3-001) is not merely unmapped but entirely unimplemented -- a symptom of the same root cause. The most accurate single label is BACKEND_BLOCKED_BY_SCHEDULE_GENERATION: backend's schedule-generation code path (PlanServices.GeneratePreviewAsync + PlaceholderPlanGenerationEngine) is explicitly documented in its own source as a 'Phase 1 placeholder' with 'no real generation logic', reads from a database schema structurally unrelated to plan-catalog, and has zero seeded content for TEN_K/Intermediate/4-day at all. No amount of plan-catalog-side work can make v10 backend-ready until this integration is built. BACKEND_READY_FOR_PILOT_SMOKE_TEST and BACKEND_READY_WITH_MANUAL_ACTIVATION_RISKS are both ruled out because there is no code path to smoke-test against v10 at all, not merely unresolved risk.
